aufstehen.story: The bed shouts AUF, but the patient only stands up at the end of the sentence. The prefix is the last one out of bed: Ich stehe um 6 Uhr auf.

stehen.story: Herr Becker stands so still that the monitor thinks he is a coat stand. stehen stays in one piece. aufstehen is the one that jumps.

anziehen.story: The hospital gown is shy. AN hides at the end of the sentence and only then does Frau Berger get dressed: Sie ziehen den Kittel an.

schmerz.story: The calf keeps one lightning bolt in a jar labelled SCHMERZ. One bolt is der Schmerz. When the jar rattles all night, it schmerzt. A quiet jar is schmerzfrei.

schmerzen.story: The calf keeps one lightning bolt in a jar labelled SCHMERZ. One bolt is der Schmerz. When the jar rattles all night, it schmerzt. A quiet jar is schmerzfrei.

schwellung.story: The right calf secretly blows up a balloon under the skin. That balloon is die Schwellung. By morning the balloon has won and the leg is geschwollen.

untersuchen.story: Dr Haddad turns the patient into a checklist. untersuchen is the looking. die Untersuchung is the appointment on the board. untersucht means the checklist is finished and can go to the Oberärztin.

tablette.story: The tablet wears a tiny white coat and refuses to work until it has had breakfast. die Tablette nach dem Essen, never on an empty stomach in this story.

patient.story: Patient sounds like 'pay shunt': the person who patiently waits while everyone else rushes. der Patient, die Patientin, and a whole ward of Patienten.

atmen.story: The lungs are two accordion players. ein is the breath they pull in, aus is the note they push out. atmen is the whole song, die Atmung is its name on the chart.

einnehmen.story: EIN is a little door into the stomach. The tablet knocks, walks through, and only then does the prefix sit down at the end: Er nimmt die Tablette ein.

abhören.story: AB means the stethoscope goes off on a tour. It listens to the lung, then the heart, and the prefix reports back at the end: Ich höre Lunge und Herz ab.

vorstellen.story: VOR means before anything clinical happens, you put your name on the table. Ich stelle mich vor. The name badge hops to the end of the sentence.

klingeln.story: The call bell is a tiny bird named Klingel. When the pain grows, the bird sings. Ich klingle. The nurse already knows the song.

verstehen.story: VER sticks to the verb like a shy intern who will not stand at the end of the sentence. verstehen stays together. If you miss a word, you ask, you do not guess.

blut.story: Blut rhymes with 'blue' only in English panic. On the ward it is the red ink in the pen of the lab. das Blut, die Blutung, der Blutdruck.

thrombose.story: Imagine a traffic jam in a vein, with one rude clot sitting in the fast lane. That jam is die Thrombose. In this lesson it is a suspicion, not a finished diagnosis.

vene.story: A vein is a blue commuter train running back to the heart. die Vene. When a medicine rides that train, it is intravenös.

fieber.story: The thermometer is a moody lighthouse. When it flashes, the patient has das Fieber. A calm lighthouse is fieberfrei.

puls.story: The pulse is a small drummer under the thumb. der Puls. If the drummer speeds up, you count before you tell the story.

verband.story: der Verband is a neat white scarf the wound wears to work. verbinden is tying that scarf. It does not split: ver stays glued on.

verbinden.story: der Verband is a neat white scarf the wound wears to work. verbinden is tying that scarf. It does not split: ver stays glued on.

wunde.story: die Wunde is a small door in the skin that should have stayed shut. Keep it clean, and let the Verband do the talking.

allergie.story: An allergy is a bouncer who hates one guest. die Allergie throws peanuts, penicillin, or pollen out of the club. Ask before you bring a new guest in.

helfen.story: helfen lends a hand and then changes its vowel, as if the hand waved: du hilfst, er hilft. The noun that stays behind is die Hilfe.

schlafen.story: schlafen steals the vowel and replaces it with a quiet ä, like a dimmed light: du schläfst. der Schlaf is the dark room itself.

trinken.story: The water jug on the locker is training for a marathon. trinken is the training. das Getränk is the medal, a very small cup.

essen.story: essen is polite until du and er arrive. Then it forgets how to spell and becomes isst, as if the soup were too hot to pronounce.

messen.story: messen brings a tape measure to the calf. The vowels panic and become i: du misst. The number you write down is die Messung.

operation.story: operieren sounds like an opera, and the theatre lights are just as bright. die Operation is the performance. Nobody improvises the ending.

operieren.story: operieren sounds like an opera, and the theatre lights are just as bright. die Operation is the performance. Nobody improvises the ending.

dokumentieren.story: If it is not in the chart, the night shift will think it never happened. dokumentieren is writing it down before you leave the room.

arzt.story: der Arzt wears the coat. die Ärztin wears the same coat and a different article. Both are ärztlich the moment the coat is on.

station.story: die Station is a small village with one corridor as its main street. People say auf Station and often leave the article at home.

bett.story: das Bett is the patient's office. Everything important — aufstehen, hochlegen, klingeln — happens at the edge of this office.

nehmen.story: nehmen hides an i in the present, like a tablet hidden in the hand: du nimmst, er nimmt. einnehmen sends that hand toward the mouth.

sehen.story: sehen grows an ie when it looks closely: du siehst, er sieht. ansehen is that look pointed at the leg, with an waiting at the end.

sprechen.story: sprechen trips over its own vowel: du sprichst. das Gespräch is the trip you take together, slowly, and you may ask for a repeat.
